text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - Taiwan's FGEP group of importers bought two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. corn at tender on Thursday. The first shipment was bought FOB at $126.00 per tonne. Shipment was slated for December 10-25 from the U.S. Gulf. The second shipment, bought from Toepfer, was bought C and F at 89.5 U.S. cents over March Chicago futures. Shipment was slated for January 10-25 from the U.S. Gulf.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - The Japanese Food Agency said on Thursday it had bought 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 60,000 of Australian wheat and 40,000 tonnes of Canadian barley at its weekly tender, all for December shipment.

VEGOIL SALE - Tunisia bought 33,000 tonnes of soyoil at $542 to $549 C&F per tonne at a tender on Thursday, traders said. Delivery is for 5-20 December 1996 and 5-20 January 1997. The tender was launched on Wednesday for up to 12,000 tonnes of soy and/or rapeseed oil by the state-buying body Office National de l'Huile.

SOYBEAN SALES - Soybean sales to China for the week ending Oct 17 totaled 287,800 tonnes, USDA said in its weekly export sales report Thursday. Soymeal sales to China were 134,000 tonnes in the same week. Soyoil sales to China totaled 20,000 tonnes in the week.

RICE SALE - The Japanese Food Agency said it bought 115,800 tonnes of rice at an import tender on Thursday. It said it bought 50,000 tonnes from the United States, 30,000 from Australia and 35,800 from Thailand. The average price was 67,823 yen per tonne, the agency said.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said on Wednesday it was extending until noon (1000 GMT) on November 6 the deadline for bids for 30,000 tonnes U.S. or Argentine yellow corn and 30,000 tonnes of soybean, any origin. The old deadline was October 30.
BARLEY TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it invited tenders by October 29 for 25,000 tonnes feed barley, for Nov 20-Dec 5 shipment from Europe or Nov 10-25 from North America.

WHEAT TENDER - A Philippine flour mill is planning to buy 20,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat if the price falls below $4 a bushel, Manila traders said on Thursday. Traders said the milling company invited tenders for 20,000 tonnes of combined spring and western white wheat.

WHEAT TENDER - Pakistan is seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. number two or better soft white wheat for November 12-30 delivery, the buyers' U.S. agent said. Bids will be opened on November 3 at 1100 local time and must remain valid until 1800 local time the following day.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria is seeking 75,000 extra tonnes of soft wheat of French and/or Argentine origin in three lots of 25,000 tonnes each, trading sources said. Shipments are set for November and December. The tender expires on Thursday.

- Egypt's official commodities buyer said on Tuesday he was inviting bids for 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat or soft white standard wheat from Australia for delivery between November 1 and 15. The deadline for bids was on Friday.
MARKET TALK - A 50,000 tonnes cargo of soybeans was sold to China last week for November delivery to the northern province of Shandong, but enquiries are beginning to thin, grain traders said.
